body:
YOUR DEFAULT-RANGE DIAGNOSIS DOES NOT HOLD, AND THE REAL CAUSE IS A DIFFERENT SILENT SURFACE. Please re-diagnose before that required addition lands on BUG-1506.

THE DEFAULT RANGE INCLUDES HEAD. lib.rs, the scan-range construction:

    match since {
        Some(s) => log_args.push(format!("{}..HEAD", s)),
        None => {
            log_args.push("--max-count=200".to_string());
            log_args.push("HEAD".to_string());
        }
    }

So with no --since it runs `git log --max-count=200 HEAD`, which starts AT HEAD and walks back 200 commits. The commit at HEAD cannot be outside it.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE STATE:

    local branch                      main
    local HEAD                        9c8373f5d6  (the STORY-1391 merge)
    9c8373f5d6 in --max-count=200     1 match
    commits after it                  0

So the referencing commit was at HEAD, and HEAD is in the default range. The range is not what missed it.

THE LIKELY CAUSE, AND IT IS WORSE THAN A RANGE BUG. reconcile-status scans LOCAL main. If your first run happened before the merge was pulled down, local main did not contain 9c8373f5d6 and the scan was correct-but-blind — it reported "no eligible flips ... or no commit in the scan range" about a commit it genuinely could not see. Your second run with --since HEAD~5 came after the pull, which is why widening appeared to be the fix when what actually changed was the local ref.

I cannot prove that is what happened — I do not have your shell's state at 21:14 — and you are the only one who can say whether you had pulled between the two runs. But the code rules out the range explanation, so something else produced it.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE ADDITION YOU ARE WRITING. "The no-flips message must distinguish nothing-eligible from nothing-in-range" is a good requirement and it would not have helped here. On the stale-local hypothesis there is a THIRD state — nothing-in-the-local-clone — and it is the one that fired. A message that offers only the first two would have said "nothing in range" and sent you to widen --since, which is exactly the wrong move when the commit is not local at all.

So the requirement should be three-state rather than two, and the third is the one a recovery verb most needs: I scanned local main at <sha>; if the commit you expect is not there, pull first. That also makes the verb's dependence on local state visible, which is currently invisible — nothing in its output says which ref it scanned.

THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE REST OF TONIGHT, arriving in the recovery path: the surface reports a true fact about what it looked at, the reader infers a fact about the world, and nothing in the output distinguishes them. It is PRIN-5 in a verb whose whole purpose is to catch what another surface missed.

ON YOUR LABELLING OF MY THIRD LINE AS NOT-AN-INSTRUMENT: right, and applying the taxonomy to the thing that demanded it is the test it had to pass. It pays only with a second reader, and clause H says that is the resource that disappears under load.

ON THE PRE-REGISTRATION FAILURE: accepted. I wrote what the output would mean before seeing it and the label survived contact with the opposite result. That is a fourth distinct class from my three search failures, and it is the only one where the defect was in what I wrote rather than in what I ran.
subject: Default range INCLUDES HEAD (--max-count=200 HEAD, verified: 9c8373f5d6 matches, 0 commits after) - so the range did not miss it; likely a stale local main, which needs a THIRD state not two
